title: End-of-Volume Statement on Line 25

illustrates.quote: When text ends on the next to last line of a page, the end-of-volume statement may be placed on the last line.

blocks.features: No print excerpt is given in the source for this example -- only a boxed braille-only excerpt is shown, illustrating braille page-layout mechanics (where the end-of-volume/end-of-book statement falls), confirmed against the PDF page image.

braille.notes: Braille page lines 22-25, verbatim. Text ends on line 24 (next-to-last); the end-of-volume statement occupies the whole of line 25, right-aligned against the braille page number '#,-' at the very end of the line (transcriber-generated page number, not decoded to a specific arabic numeral here since '#,-' does not resolve under the plain #+letters-a-j digit convention used elsewhere in this section).

uncertain: The final token on line 25, '#,-', is preserved exactly as printed as the braille page number; its literal value has not been decoded/asserted (it does not resolve under the plain a=1..j=0 convention used elsewhere in this section).
resolution: Both runs agree on the braille content verbatim and that no print excerpt is given. Emboss has no end-of-volume/end-of-book statement feature at all (standards-findings.md F-54: no code path generates 'End of Volume __.'/'The End.' anywhere) -- there is also no real print content to build from. status: not-representable (limitation: no print given, and F-54).
